heroHeadline: MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Day 20; UN Confirms 1.5M Displaced; GSF Full Operations Launch in 3 Days as HRP Only 23% Funded
heroSubtitle: On May 29, 2026, the United Nations confirmed that approximately 1.5 million Haitians are now internally displaced — with the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area crossing 300,000 IDPs for the first time — as the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan remains only 23% funded ($198.7 million of $880 million secured). MSF's hospital in Cité Soleil enters its 20th consecutive day of forced closure on May 29, the longest documented uninterrupted shutdown since the crisis began, leaving approximately 300,000 commune residents without emergency medical access. The Gang Suppression Force — with its advance contingent of approximately 800 personnel (less than 15% of the 5,500-person authorized ceiling) — is scheduled to launch full operations June 1, three days away, but the force is concentrated exclusively in Port-au-Prince's city center with no coverage for Cité Soleil, Martissant, or the Artibonite. On May 27, Haiti inaugurated its first specialized judicial units: two panels of 25 magistrates each — one for mass crimes, sexual violence, kidnapping, and trafficking; the other for financial crimes and electoral fraud — which PM Fils-Aimé marked with the declaration 'The law prevails over guns.' Human rights groups noted both units' jurisdiction is limited to Port-au-Prince's Court of First Instance, excluding the departments where the worst atrocities have occurred. The US Supreme Court ruling on TPS for approximately 350,000 Haitian nationals — in Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot — remains expected before late June 2026; Senate advocates are pushing a standalone bill to extend TPS through 2027 ahead of the ruling.
